skill.name: send-experiment-designer
skill.description: Designs email A/B, multivariate, send-time, and hold-out tests with hypotheses, variant matrices, sample plans, and significance read-outs.
skill.summary: Plan email send experiments and make evidence-based promote, kill, or keep-testing decisions.
skill.author: aaron-he-zhu

security_audit.summary: Most static detections are false positives from Markdown backticks, fenced prompt examples, connector placeholders, and fixed repo-relative documentation links. I confirmed only the optional local experiment.py and python3 statistical helper references as external command surfaces; no prompt injection, network exfiltration, or dynamic path traversal evidence was found.

remediation.issue: Optional statistical helper uses external command execution.
remediation.suggestion: Document the expected script path, require numeric arguments, and provide a no-command formula fallback for hosts that block execution.

remediation.issue: Parent-directory documentation links trigger path traversal scanners.
remediation.suggestion: Package referenced materials with the skill or replace parent-directory links with stable skill-local references.

remediation.issue: The skill can save experiment summaries to memory after consent.
remediation.suggestion: Keep the explicit consent step and avoid storing raw ESP exports, customer data, or revenue records in memory.

content.value_statement: Email teams often run tests that are underpowered or hard to interpret. This skill creates disciplined send experiments and clear read-outs from ESP results.
actual_capabilities: Selects A/B, multivariate, send-time, or hold-out mode from the request.
Writes a falsifiable email experiment hypothesis with one changed variable.
Builds variant matrices with controls and guardrail metrics.
Estimates sample size, minimum detectable effect, duration, and power.
Reads finished ESP exports and returns promote, kill, or keep-testing decisions.
Labels numbers as measured, user-provided, or estimated.
limitations: It does not write subject lines, body copy, or creative assets.
It needs baseline rates, list size, or an ESP export for strong recommendations.
Small lists may only detect large effects or require longer runs.
It does not replace legal, privacy, or deliverability review.

use_cases.title: Plan a Subject-Line Test
use_cases.description: Create a controlled A/B plan with baseline open rate, detectable lift, sample size, duration, and guardrails.

use_cases.title: Compare Send Times
use_cases.description: Design a send-time test that holds segment, creative, and subject constant while comparing same-window engagement.

use_cases.title: Read a Finished Experiment
use_cases.description: Use exported delivered, open, click, and conversion counts to decide whether to promote, kill, or keep testing.

prompt_templates.title: Basic A/B Plan
prompt_templates.scenario: A beginner needs a two-cell test plan.
prompt_templates.prompt: Design an A/B subject-line test. Baseline open rate is 38 percent, target lift is 3 points, list size is 12,000, and goal is retention.

prompt_templates.title: Send-Time Plan
prompt_templates.scenario: A marketer needs a controlled timing experiment.
prompt_templates.prompt: Build a send-time test for a weekly newsletter. Baseline open rate is 40 percent, list size is 20,000, and I can send over one week.

prompt_templates.title: Multivariate Reality Check
prompt_templates.scenario: A team wants to know if a larger design is powered.
prompt_templates.prompt: Evaluate a 2 by 2 subject and CTA test. Baseline click rate is 2.1 percent, list size is 60,000, and minimum lift is 0.5 points.

prompt_templates.title: Finished Test Read-Out
prompt_templates.scenario: An analyst has completed test results.
prompt_templates.prompt: Read this finished email test and decide promote, kill, or keep testing. I have delivered counts, opens, clicks, conversions, and guardrail rates by variant.

output_examples.input: Plan a subject-line A/B test with 12,000 recipients and a 38 percent baseline open rate.
output_examples.output: The skill returns a two-cell design, one changed subject variable, sample needs per cell, run duration, and unsubscribe guardrails.

output_examples.input: Read a completed CTA test with delivered, click, and conversion counts by variant.
output_examples.output: The skill names the significance method, reports lift against the planned threshold, and gives a promote, kill, or keep-testing decision.

output_examples.input: Design a hold-out test to measure incremental revenue from a campaign.
output_examples.output: The skill defines a no-send control, powers the test on conversion or revenue baseline, and explains how to read incremental lift.

best_practices: Provide baseline rate, list size, sendable volume per day, and minimum practical lift.
Change only one variable per cell so the winner is attributable.
Set sample size and read date before launch, then avoid early winner calls.
anti_patterns: Do not change subject, creative, and CTA in one A/B cell.
Do not promote a winner on observed lift without significance and practical lift.
Do not use open-rate power plans for hold-out tests measured on conversion.

faq.question: Can this skill write the email copy?
faq.answer: No. It designs the experiment and reads results. Use a creative writing skill for subject lines, body copy, and CTAs.

faq.question: What inputs should I provide?
faq.answer: Provide the test goal, baseline rate, list size, send volume, target lift, and any finished ESP export counts.

faq.question: Does it support multivariate tests?
faq.answer: Yes. It can design crossed tests, but it checks that every cell has enough sample size.

faq.question: Can it analyze a finished test?
faq.answer: Yes. It can read delivered, open, click, conversion, and guardrail counts to make a decision.

faq.question: What happens when my list is too small?
faq.answer: It recommends a larger detectable lift, a longer run, fewer cells, or not running the test.

faq.question: Does it need API access to my ESP?
faq.answer: No. Manual exports are enough. Any keyed ESP connector is optional and not required.
